import jobs

# Test stable deduplication by (source, source_id)
def test_unique_jobs():
    # Test case 1: Basic deduplication by (source, source_id)
    rows = [
        {'title': 'Job A', 'source': 'X', 'source_id': '1'},
        {'title': 'Job B', 'source': 'X', 'source_id': '1'},  # Duplicate source_id
        {'title': 'Job C', 'source': 'Y', 'source_id': '2'},
        {'title': 'Job D', 'source': 'X', 'source_id': '2'},
        {'title': 'Job E', 'source': 'X', 'source_id': ''},  # Empty source_id
        {'title': 'Job F', 'source': '', 'source_id': '3'},  # Empty source
        {'title': 'Job G', 'source': '', 'source_id': ''},  # Both empty
        {'title': 'Job H', 'source': 'X', 'source_id': None},  # None source_id
    ]
    unique = jobs.unique_jobs(rows)
    
    # Check deduplication by (source, source_id) and stability (first occurrence kept)
    expected_keys = [
        ('X', '1'), ('Y', '2'), ('X', '2'), ('X', ''), ('', '3'), ('', ''), ('X', None)
    ]
    assert len(unique) == len(expected_keys), f"Expected {len(expected_keys)} unique rows, got {len(unique)}"
    
    # Verify no title-based merging
    titles = {row['title'] for row in unique}
    assert len(titles) == len(rows), "Titles should not be merged"
    
    # Verify no merging across sources (only by (source, source_id))
    for i, row in enumerate(unique):
        key = (row.get('source', ''), row.get('source_id', ''))
        assert key == expected_keys[i], f"Row {i} has incorrect (source, source_id) key: {key}, expected {expected_keys[i]}"

if __name__ == '__main__':
    test_unique_jobs()
